# Language

Every built-in thing you can write in PDL — frames, token types, emits, protocols, samples — with a locked meaning. Look up a type here when you want to know what it is and when to use it. Names you declare with `variant` / `enum` are yours — see Variants.

Language **1.0.0-beta**.

## Declarations {#declarations}

The top-level blocks in a `.pdl` file. Use them to import files, name tokens, and define components. Order inside a file is free.

| Name | Form | Meaning |
|------|------|------|
| [`import`](#files) | `import "relative/path.pdl"` | Pull another file into this design. Paths are relative to the importing file. There is no export — names are visible after merge. Later files win for themes and components; a second token of the same name is PDL-E003. Cycles are PDL-E002. |
| `previewBackground` | `previewBackground = color.token` | The preview canvas color. Use a [`Color`](#color) token, not a layout property. |
| `primitive` | `primitive name: Type = …` | A raw palette value (`#3B82F6`, `12`). Components should use semantic names instead. |
| `semantic` | `semantic name: Type = …` | An intent name components should use ([`color.surface`](#color), `space.stack`). Points at a primitive or another semantic. |
| [`theme`](#theme) | `theme Name { token = value … }` | A named remap of tokens — light, dark, reduced motion. Body lines assign existing token names. Themes do not inherit from each other. |
| [`typeStyle`](#typestyle) | `typeStyle Name { … }` | A named bundle of text-frame properties. A text frame sets `style = Title`. See [`typeStyle`](#typestyle). |
| [`variant`](#variants) | `variant Name { case a; case b }` | A closed set of visual choices (tone, size). Write `.primary` at use sites. Same as enum in v1. |
| [`enum`](#variants) | `enum Name { case a; case b }` | Same as variant in v1. Prefer [`enum`](#variants) for ids (`FilterId`); prefer [`variant`](#variants) for visual axes. |
| `protocol` | `protocol P: component { … }  or  protocol P { host … }` | A shared contract. Use an API protocol so mixed chips share `select`; use a host protocol so the preview can deliver clicks. |
| `component` | `component Name(params) kind { … }` | A reusable UI piece: a name, public parameters, and one root frame. |
| `emits` | `emits Name { channel(field: Type) }  or  } emits { … }` | What this component can tell its parent (selected, changed). Not a click from the preview — that is a host event. |
| [`fixtures`](#fixtures) | `fixtures Component { example "Label" { param = value } }` | Named preview scenarios (“Empty search”, “Focus mood”). A bag of parameters — not data you put on screen. |
| `samples` | `samples Bank { entry { field: Type = … } }` | A reusable catalog of instances you mount so a prototype can stay interactive. Point at `Tracks.library.tracks`. |
| [`usage`](#usage) | `usage Component { description = "…" }` | A written note for authors and tools. In v1 the only key is `description`. See [`Usage`](#usage). |
| [`rules`](#rule) | `rules Component { tags = […]; Rule(.must, …) }` | Checks the design can fail in preview or CI. Tags and [`Rule`](#rule) lines live only here. See [`Rule`](#rule). |
| [`extend`](#extend) | `extend Component { fixtures { … } usage { … } rules { … } }` | Add fixtures, usage, or rules to an imported component without copying its layout. See [`Extend`](#extend). |

```pdl
import "tokens.pdl"
previewBackground color.surface

component Greeting(title: String = "Hello") layout {
  let heading = Text(content: title, style: Title)
  children = [heading]
}
```

## Files and import {#files}

The entry `.pdl` file is the root of the merged design. `import "relative/path.pdl"` pulls another module. There is no export — after merge, names are just names. Paths are relative to the importing file. Token names (`primitive` / `semantic`) are unique across the graph (PDL-E003). Themes, components, and most other top-level kinds: later wins. Import cycles are PDL-E002. The entry file’s own declarations merge last.

Accepted syntax:

- `import "design/tokens.pdl"` — Relative to this file. Merges that module into the design.
- `previewBackground = color.surface` — Canvas color for preview. A [`Color`](#color) token, not a layout property.

Rejected:

- `export component Card` — There is no export keyword. Import the file that declares the name.
- `import "a.pdl" that imports this file` — Cycles are PDL-E002.
- `primitive color.ink: Color = #111 in two files` — Token redeclaration is PDL-E003.

```pdl
previewBackground = color.surface

import "design/tokens.pdl"
import "design/themes.pdl"
import "design/buttons.pdl"
```

## Syntax {#syntax}

Identifiers are letters, digits, `_`, and `.` where the grammar allows (`MyComponent`, `color.text.primary`). Line comments are `// …`. Block comments are `/* … */`. Hex colors are not strings — write `#RRGGBB`, not `"#RRGGBB"`. Numbers are unitless; there is no `px` suffix.

Accepted syntax:

- `// line comment` — To end of line. Treated as whitespace.
- `/* block */` — May span lines.
- `#1E293B` — A [`Color`](#color) literal, not a string.
- `12` — Unitless number. [`Distance`](#distance) and [`Size`](#size) are design units (pixels in HTML preview).

Rejected:

- `"#1E293B"` — Quoted hex is PDL-E017.
- `12px` — No unit suffix.

```pdl
// Shared palette
primitive color.ink: Color = #111827  // inline

/*
  Block comment.
*/
component Note() layout {
  gap = 12
}
```

## Frames

Every component has one root frame. Nested UI is the same four constructors on [`let`](#let). Use [`layout`](#layout) to group, [`text`](#text) for words, [`icon`](#icon-frame) for a glyph, [`media`](#media-frame) for an image or video. Unknown properties are PDL-E011; wrong types are PDL-E006.

### Layout {#layout}

A flex-like container — the usual root of a component, and any nested group. Write `component Card layout { … }` for the root, or `let box = Layout(…)` for a nested group. Set [`direction`](#direction) to [`.row`](#direction) or [`.column`](#direction) (or [`.stack`](#direction) to overlap). Named children go in [`children`](#children). Spacing is `gap` / `padding` ([`Distance`](#distance) and [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets)). Alignment is [`align`](#align) and [`justify`](#justify).

| Property | Type | Values |
|----------|------|--------|
| `align` | [`Align`](#align) | [`.start`](#align) · [`.center`](#align) · [`.end`](#align) · [`.stretch`](#align) |
| `background` | [`Color`](#color), [`Background`](#background), [`Foreground`](#foreground), [`Ramp`](#ramp), [`Blur`](#blur), [`Media`](#media), [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy) | hex, opacityOf, array |
| `borderColor` | [`Color`](#color) | hex, opacityOf |
| `borderPosition` | [`BorderPosition`](#borderposition) | [`.inside`](#borderposition) · [`.outside`](#borderposition) |
| `borderWidth` | `nonNegNumber` | ≥ 0 |
| `columnGap` | [`Distance`](#distance) | ≥ 0 |
| `cornerRadius` | [`Radius`](#radius), [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii) | ≥ 0 |
| `direction` | [`Direction`](#direction) | [`.row`](#direction) · [`.column`](#direction) · [`.rowReverse`](#direction) · [`.columnReverse`](#direction) · [`.stack`](#direction) · [`.reverseStack`](#direction) |
| `foreground` | [`Color`](#color), [`Background`](#background), [`Foreground`](#foreground), [`Ramp`](#ramp), [`Blur`](#blur), [`Media`](#media), [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy) | hex, opacityOf, array |
| `gap` | [`Distance`](#distance) | ≥ 0 |
| `height` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |
| `hidden` | `Bool` or condition | boolean, condition |
| `justify` | [`Justify`](#justify) | [`.start`](#justify) · [`.center`](#justify) · [`.end`](#justify) · [`.stretch`](#justify) · [`.spaceBetween`](#justify) · [`.spaceAround`](#justify) |
| `margin` | [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets) | ≥ 0 |
| `opacity` | [`Opacity`](#opacity) | 0…1 |
| `overflow` | [`Overflow`](#overflow) | [`.visible`](#overflow) · [`.scroll`](#overflow) · [`.clip`](#overflow) |
| `padding` | [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets) | ≥ 0 |
| `rowGap` | [`Distance`](#distance) | ≥ 0 |
| `shadow` | [`Shadow`](#shadow) | shadow |
| `width` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |
| `wrap` | [`Wrap`](#wrap) | [`.nowrap`](#wrap) · [`.wrap`](#wrap) |

```pdl
component Card layout {
  direction = .column
  gap = 8
  padding = 16
  let title = Text(content: "Hello")
  children = [title]
}
```

### Text {#text}

A typography node. `content` is the string. Prefer `style:` naming a [`typeStyle`](#typestyle) for size and weight; override with [`color`](#color), `fontSize`, and the other text properties when needed. Root form is `component Title text { … }`; nested form is `let heading = Text(…)`.

| Property | Type | Values |
|----------|------|--------|
| `align` | [`Align`](#align) | [`.start`](#align) · [`.center`](#align) · [`.end`](#align) |
| `background` | [`Color`](#color), [`Background`](#background), [`Foreground`](#foreground), [`Ramp`](#ramp), [`Blur`](#blur), [`Media`](#media), [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy) | hex, opacityOf, array |
| `borderColor` | [`Color`](#color) | hex, opacityOf |
| `borderPosition` | [`BorderPosition`](#borderposition) | [`.inside`](#borderposition) · [`.outside`](#borderposition) |
| `borderWidth` | `nonNegNumber` | ≥ 0 |
| `color` | [`Color`](#color) | hex, opacityOf |
| `content` | [`String`](#string) | string |
| `cornerRadius` | [`Radius`](#radius), [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii) | ≥ 0 |
| `editable` | `structural` | — |
| `fontFamily` | [`FontFamily`](#fontfamily) | string |
| `fontSize` | [`Size`](#size) | ≥ 0 |
| `fontWeight` | [`Weight`](#weight) | number |
| `foreground` | [`Color`](#color), [`Background`](#background), [`Foreground`](#foreground), [`Ramp`](#ramp), [`Blur`](#blur), [`Media`](#media), [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy) | hex, opacityOf, array |
| `height` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |
| `justify` | [`Justify`](#justify) | [`.start`](#justify) · [`.center`](#justify) · [`.end`](#justify) |
| `letterSpacing` | [`LetterSpacing`](#letterspacing) | number |
| `lineClamp` | `nonNegNumber` | ≥ 0 |
| `lineHeight` | [`LineHeight`](#lineheight) | > 0 |
| `margin` | [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets) | ≥ 0 |
| `opacity` | [`Opacity`](#opacity) | 0…1 |
| `overflow` | [`Overflow`](#overflow) | [`.visible`](#overflow) · [`.scroll`](#overflow) · [`.clip`](#overflow) |
| `padding` | [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets) | ≥ 0 |
| `shadow` | [`Shadow`](#shadow) | shadow |
| `style` | [`typeStyle`](#typestyle) | — |
| `truncateStyle` | [`TruncateStyle`](#truncatestyle) | [`.clip`](#truncatestyle) · [`.ellipsis`](#truncatestyle) |
| `width` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |

```pdl
let heading = Text(content: title, style: Title, color: color.text)
```

### Icon {#icon-frame}

A small tintable glyph. The `icon` property is an [`Icon`](#icon) token or [`IconRef`](#iconref) — not this frame. Set [`size`](#size) or `width` / `height`. Tint with [`color`](#color). Nested form is `let star = Icon(…)`.

| Property | Type | Values |
|----------|------|--------|
| `color` | [`Color`](#color) | hex, opacityOf |
| `height` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |
| `icon` | [`Icon`](#icon) | string, iconRef |
| `opacity` | [`Opacity`](#opacity) | 0…1 |
| `size` | [`Size`](#size) | ≥ 0 |
| `width` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |

```pdl
let star = Icon(icon: IconRef(system: .sfSymbols, name: "star"), size: 16, color: color.ink)
```

### Media {#media-frame}

A box that draws raster, vector, or video from a [`MediaSource`](#mediasource). Distinct from [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer), which is a fill inside [`background`](#background) / [`foreground`](#foreground). Fit the source with [`contentMode`](#contentmode) ([`.cover`](#contentmode), [`.contain`](#contentmode), …). Nested form is `let photo = Media(…)`.

| Property | Type | Values |
|----------|------|--------|
| `align` | [`Align`](#align) | [`.start`](#align) · [`.center`](#align) · [`.end`](#align) |
| `aspectRatio` | [`Ratio`](#ratio) | number, ratio |
| `background` | [`Color`](#color), [`Background`](#background), [`Foreground`](#foreground), [`Ramp`](#ramp), [`Blur`](#blur), [`Media`](#media), [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy) | hex, opacityOf, array |
| `contentMode` | [`ContentMode`](#contentmode) | [`.cover`](#contentmode) · [`.contain`](#contentmode) · [`.fill`](#contentmode) · [`.scaleDown`](#contentmode) |
| `cornerRadius` | [`Radius`](#radius), [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii) | ≥ 0 |
| `foreground` | [`Color`](#color), [`Background`](#background), [`Foreground`](#foreground), [`Ramp`](#ramp), [`Blur`](#blur), [`Media`](#media), [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy) | hex, opacityOf, array |
| `height` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |
| `justify` | [`Justify`](#justify) | [`.start`](#justify) · [`.center`](#justify) · [`.end`](#justify) |
| `opacity` | [`Opacity`](#opacity) | 0…1 |
| `source` | [`MediaSource`](#mediasource) | string, mediaSourceRef |
| `width` | [`Sizing`](#sizing) | ≥ 0 · [`.hug`](#sizing) · [`.fill`](#sizing) · `.fixed(n)` |

```pdl
let photo = Media(source: media.hero, contentMode: .cover, height: 120)
```

## Children {#children}

[`children`](#children) belongs on [`Layout`](#layout) — that is how PDL draws views and nested views. A child [`Layout`](#layout) has its own [`children`](#children). [`Text()`](#text), [`Icon()`](#icon-frame), and [`Media()`](#media-frame) are leaves: they do not take [`children`](#children) and do not nest views. Every entry is a component — a built-in frame or one you declared (`Button(…)`). Name them with [`let`](#let), then mount them with `children = [heading, save]`. A [`let`](#let) that never appears in [`children`](#children) is not drawn. [`Spacer()`](#spacer) is the leftover-space exception. A [`ForEach`](#foreach) block does not mount views by itself.

```pdl
component Button(label: String = "OK") layout {
  padding = 12
  background = #2563EB
  cornerRadius = 8

  let text = Text(content: label, color: #FFFFFF)
  children = [text]
}

component Card(title: String = "Hello") layout {
  direction = .column
  gap = 8

  let heading = Text(content: title)
  let save = Button(label: "Save")

  children = [heading, save]
}
```

Child properties sit on the **child** of a [`Layout`](#layout) (constructor args or after the `let`), not on the parent. A [`text`](#text) / [`icon`](#icon-frame) / [`media`](#media-frame) root does not take these unless a property table says so.

| Property | Type | Values |
|----------|------|--------|
| `alignSelf` | [`AlignSelf`](#alignself) | [`.start`](#alignself) · [`.center`](#alignself) · [`.end`](#alignself) · [`.stretch`](#alignself) · [`.auto`](#alignself) |
| `grow` | `number` | number |
| `inset` | [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets) | ≥ 0 |
| `position` | [`Position`](#position) | [`.flow`](#position) · [`.absolute`](#position) |
| `shrink` | `number` | number |

## Spacer {#spacer}

A child that eats leftover space on the main axis. Write `Spacer()` inside `children = […]`.

Zero-argument child that absorbs remaining free space on the parent’s main axis. Only legal inside `children = […]`. Write `Spacer()` — bare `Spacer` is a name. `Spacer() @ opacity` is illegal.

```pdl
component Toolbar() layout {
  direction = .row
  align = .center

  let title = Text(content: "Library")
  let action = Text(content: "Edit")

  children = [title, Spacer(), action]
}
```

## Array children {#arraychildren}

A list parameter (`chips: [FilterChip]`) mounts when it appears in [`children`](#children). `children = chips` and `children = [chips]` both splice the list in place. Mix siblings with brackets: `children = [header, chips, footer]`. A single slot (`content: ModalContent = UpsellBody()`) also expands in [`children`](#children). Dotted override `slot.field = value` is legal on a single slot — if `field` is a param it overrides the instance; otherwise it sets a root-frame prop. Array slots cannot use `slots.foo =` (PDL-E034); use [`ForEach`](#foreach).

Accepted syntax:

- `children = chips` — Mount the list. Same as `children = [chips]`.
- `children = [header, chips, footer]` — Compose: lists splice among siblings.

Rejected:

- `slots.title = "X"` — Dotted override on an array slot is PDL-E034. Use [`ForEach`](#foreach).

```pdl
component Modal(
  chromeTitle: String = "Dialog",
  slots: [ModalContent] = [UpsellBody()]
) layout {
  let header = Text(content: chromeTitle)
  children = [header, slots]
}
```

## ForEach

Use [`ForEach`](#foreach) when a list needs per-row state or click handling — which chip is selected, which row is highlighted. It writes onto items you already put in [`children`](#children). It does not create views by itself.

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `ForEach(chips) { chip in … }` | For each item in the list, write overrides and listen for clicks. The name `chip` is the current item. |
| `children = chips` | Put the list on screen. [`ForEach`](#foreach) does not do this by itself. Use brackets when mixing siblings: `[Header, chips, Footer]`. |
| `chip.selected = self.currentFilter == filter` | Set each item from parent state — which chip looks selected. Use `self.` when the parent and item share a name. |
| `chip.select(filter_id: FilterId) = { … }` | Hear that item’s emit. Write `chip.select`, not `chips.select`. |
| `if self.currentFilter == filter { chip.selected = true } else { … }` | Same [`if`](#conditionals) / [`else`](#conditionals) as layout, evaluated per list item. Prefer `chip.selected = self.currentFilter == filter` when one [`Bool`](#bool) is enough. |
| `before { … } / between { … } / after { … }` | Reserved list chrome. Compilers reject these (PDL-E026). Do not invent dividers this way. |

```pdl
component LibrarySubnav(
  currentFilter: FilterId = .all,
  chips: [FilterChip] = [
    FilterChip(title: "All", filter: .all),
    FilterChip(title: "Pop", filter: .pop)
  ]
) layout {
  ForEach(chips) { chip in
    chip.selected = self.currentFilter == filter
    chip.select(filter_id: FilterId) = {
      currentFilter = filter_id
    }
  }
  children = chips
}
```

## Let {#let}

Name a nested frame, or a typed value you reuse in props. Prefer a lowercase id (`let title`, `let ramp`) so the name is not the same word as the type. Frame lets go in [`children`](#children). Typed value lets do not.

A `let` names something inside a component. Prefer a lowercase id so it does not look like the type: `let title = Text(…)` is a nested frame you mount in [`children`](#children). `let save = Button(label: "Save")` is a component you declared — instantiate it in a layout the same way. `let ramp: Ramp = Ramp(…)` is a typed value you reuse in props or layers — it is not a view and must not appear in [`children`](#children). The id must be unique in the component. Write the `let` before any `children = [id]` or `id.prop` that names it (PDL-E019).

Accepted syntax:

- `let title = Text(…)` — Nested text frame. Mount with `children = [title]`.
- `let box = Layout(…)` — Nested layout. Same four constructors as the root: [`Layout`](#layout), [`Text`](#text), [`Icon`](#icon), [`Media`](#media).
- `let save = Button(label: "Save")` — A component you declared. Pass its parameters; mount it in [`children`](#children) like a frame.
- `let ramp: Ramp = Ramp(…)` — Typed value. Reuse in `background = [ramp]`. Not mountable.
- `title.color = color.ink` — Assign after the let. The let must appear earlier in the body.

Rejected:

- `let id: text = { … }` — Classic kind-colon form is removed (PDL-E001). Use `let id = Text(…)`.
- `children = [ramp]` — A typed value let is not a frame. Put it on a property, not in children.

```pdl
component Button(label: String = "OK") layout {
  padding = 12
  background = #2563EB
  cornerRadius = 8

  let text = Text(content: label, color: #FFFFFF)
  children = [text]
}

component Card() layout {
  direction = .column
  gap = 8

  let title = Text(content: "Hello")
  let save = Button(label: "Save")
  let ramp: Ramp = Ramp(
    direction: .bottomToTop,
    stops: [
      GradientStop(color: #F00, opacity: 1, position: 0),
      GradientStop(color: #00F, opacity: 1, position: 1)
    ]
  )

  background = [ramp]
  children = [title, save]
}
```

## Parameters {#parameters}

The public inbound API of a component. Every name in the parentheses is public. There is no private parameter.

Every name in `component Name(…)` is public inbound surface. Write `name: Type = default`. Types are [`String`](#string), [`Number`](#number), [`Bool`](#bool), a token type, a variant/enum you declared, a component or protocol name, or `[Type]` for a list of instances. There is no private parameter and no `expose` filter.

Accepted syntax:

- `label: String = "Chip"` — Quoted string default.
- `selected: Bool = false` — Boolean. Write [`Bool`](#bool), not `Boolean`.
- `tone: BannerTone = .success` — A variant/enum you declared. Default is a `.case`.
- `gap: Distance = 8` — Token or value builtin, with a literal or token default.
- `content: ModalContent = UpsellBody()` — Single slot — a component or protocol instance.
- `chips: [FilterChip] = [FilterChip()]` — List of instances. Empty `[]` is allowed.

Rejected:

- `on: Boolean = false` — `Boolean` is PDL-E039. Write [`Bool`](#bool).

```pdl
enum BannerTone {
  case success
  case warning
}

component Chip(
  label: String = "Chip",
  selected: Bool = false,
  tone: BannerTone = .success
) layout {
  if tone == .success {
    background = #16A34A
  } else {
    background = #DC2626
  }

  let text = Text(content: label, color: #FFFFFF)
  children = [text]
}
```

### `String`

Quoted text. Component parameters, text content, font family, easing strings.

### `Number`

A finite number. Unitless unless the property says otherwise ([`Duration`](#duration) is milliseconds; [`Opacity`](#opacity) is 0…1; [`LineHeight`](#lineheight) is a ratio).

### `Bool`

true or false. Write `Bool`, not `Boolean` (PDL-E039).

A list of instances is `[ComponentName]` (or `[SomeProtocol]`).

## Variants {#variants}

Closed sets you declare — tone, size, filter id. Write `.case` at use sites. `enum` and `variant` are the same in v1.

A `variant` (and `enum`, the same construct in v1) is a finite set of named cases. Use it as a parameter type and in conditions. Case names are identifiers without dots. At use sites write `.caseName`. Prefer `variant` for visual axes (tone, size); prefer `enum` for ids and state sets. Tooling may treat the keywords differently later.

Accepted syntax:

- `variant BannerTone { case success; case warning }` — Declare cases. Semicolons or newlines are fine.
- `enum FilterId { case all; case pop }` — Same as variant in v1.
- `tone: BannerTone = .success` — Parameter type and `.case` default.
- `if tone == .warning { … }` — Compare to a case in a condition.

Rejected:

- `tone = success` — Cases need the leading dot: `.success`.

```pdl
variant BannerTone {
  case success
  case warning
  case danger
}

enum FilterId {
  case all
  case podcasts
}

component StatusBanner(
  label: String = "Fine",
  tone: BannerTone = .success
) layout {
  if tone == .warning {
    background = color.warn
  }
  let text = Text(content: label)
  children = [text]
}
```

## self {#self}

The enclosing component instance. Use `self.param` when a nested name would shadow. Rules-query `self` is a different thing.

`self` is the enclosing component instance — not a frame id. `self.param` in a value or condition names that component’s parameter (the escape hatch when a [`ForEach`](#foreach) item field would shadow). `self.prop = value` (not a brace block) sets a root-frame property. `self.channel = { … }` is a host inbound handler (`self.` is optional in the kind body). Inside [`rules`](#rule), `self` is the instance whose rules block is running — a different namespace.

Accepted syntax:

- `self.currentFilter` — Enclosing component parameter. Prefer this in [`ForEach`](#foreach) when the item might shadow the name.
- `self.background = #333` — Root frame property of this component — never an intermediate let.
- `self.pressEnd = { … }` — Host inbound handler. Bare `pressEnd = { … }` is the same in the kind body.
- `Rule(.should, self == parent.children.last, description: "…")` — Rules-query `self` — the instance being checked, not layout `self`.

Rejected:

- `children = [self]` — `self` is not a frame id. Mount lets and slots, not `self`.

```pdl
component LibrarySubnav(
  currentFilter: FilterId = .all,
  chips: [FilterChip] = [FilterChip(filter: .all)]
) layout {
  ForEach(chips) { chip in
    chip.selected = self.currentFilter == filter
  }
  self.background = color.surface
  children = chips
}
```

## Conditionals {#conditionals}

Change a handful of properties when a parameter or state changes. First match wins.

An `if` / `else if` / `else` chain overrides properties when a parameter or state matches. The resolver walks top to bottom and applies only the first matching branch — there is no fall-through. A branch is a flat list of assignments, not a script. Bare `prop = value` updates the enclosing frame (usually the root). `id.prop = value` updates a let. Write the let before any `id.prop` or `children = [id]` (PDL-E019).

Accepted syntax:

- `if tone == .warning { background = color.warn }` — First-match branch. Typical condition is `param == .case`.
- `else if tone == .danger { … }` — Tried only when earlier branches missed.
- `else { … }` — No condition. Runs when nothing above matched. Omit it when the frame defaults already express the base state.
- `statusIcon.color = color.accent` — Dotted assign on a let. Prefer this over nesting `if` inside a constructor.
- `if selected { … }` — A [`Bool`](#bool) parameter is truthy as a condition.

Rejected:

- `if a { … } if a { … }` — Two separate `if`s both run when they match. A chain is first-match only; later `else if` arms do not also apply.
- `children = [title] … let title = Text(…)` — Forward reference. The let must appear first (PDL-E019).

```pdl
enum InteractionState {
  case rest
  case hovered
  case pressed
}

component InteractiveChip(
  label: String = "Chip",
  interactionState: InteractionState = .rest
) layout {
  background = color.button.rest

  if interactionState == .hovered {
    background = color.button.hover
  } else if interactionState == .pressed {
    background = color.button.press
  }

  let text = Text(content: label)
  children = [text]
}
```

## Conditions {#conditions}

Comparisons and booleans used in [`if`](#conditionals) and [`ForEach`](#foreach). Keep `&&` and `||` in separate expressions, or parenthesize.

What you write after [`if`](#conditionals) (and inside [`ForEach`](#foreach)). Compare a parameter to a `.case`, test a [`Bool`](#bool), negate, or combine with `&&` / `||`. Do not mix `&&` and `||` in one expression without parentheses.

Accepted syntax:

- `tone == .warning` — Parameter equals a variant case.
- `self.currentFilter == filter` — Same-type compare. `self.` is the enclosing component; bare `filter` is often a [`ForEach`](#foreach) item field.
- `selected` — A [`Bool`](#bool) is truthy on its own.
- `!selected` — Negation.
- `a && b` — Both. Do not mix with `||` unless you parenthesize.
- `a || b` — Either. Do not mix with `&&` unless you parenthesize.

Rejected:

- `a && b || c` — Ambiguous. Write `(a && b) || c` or `a && (b || c)`.

```pdl
variant BannerTone {
  case success
  case warning
}

component Flag(on: Bool = false, tone: BannerTone = .success) layout {
  if on && tone == .warning {
    background = color.warn
  }
}
```

## null {#null}

Clear a frame or [`typeStyle`](#typestyle) property so the default applies. Not a token value.

The word `null` means pretend this property was never set. Use it on a frame or [`typeStyle`](#typestyle) property to erase a prior value so the default applies. It is not a [`Color`](#color), [`Opacity`](#opacity), or other token. `gap = null` clears `gap` only — it does not clear `columnGap` or `rowGap`.

Accepted syntax:

- `borderColor = null` — Unset. Often means absent (no border color).
- `style = null` — Clear the type-style binding on a text frame.
- `color = null` — After `style = Title`, clears that property even if the style contributed it.
- `gap = null` — Unsets `gap` only. Does not clear `columnGap` / `rowGap`.

Rejected:

- `primitive color.none: Color = null` — Not a token RHS (PDL-E005). Use a domain empty such as `borderWidth = 0` when that is the value.

```pdl
component Cleared() layout {
  borderColor = #0066FF
  borderColor = null
}
```

## Token types

Named values you declare once and reuse. Write `primitive` for the raw palette and `semantic` for the names components should use ([`color.surface`](#color)). Pick a type when a property needs a color, a gap, a shadow, and so on. [`Duration`](#duration), [`Easing`](#easing), and [`Transition`](#transition) are draft — they exist for handler motion, which is not finished.

### `Color`

A fill, text, or border color. Hex is a color, not a string.

Category: color. Used on: [`background`](#background), [`foreground`](#foreground), [`color`](#color), `borderColor`, [`Shadow`](#shadow).[`color`](#color).

Accepted syntax:

- `#RGB` — Three-digit hex.
- `#RRGGBB` — Six-digit hex. The usual literal.
- `#RRGGBBAA` — Eight-digit hex; last pair is alpha.
- `color.token` — A Color token (semantic on components).
- `color @ 0.4` — Tint: multiply alpha. Prefer an [`Opacity`](#opacity) token on the right.
- `color @ opacity.scrim` — Tint with a named [`Opacity`](#opacity).

Rejected:

- `"#3B82F6"` — Quoted hex is PDL-E017.

```pdl
primitive color.primitive.blue.500: Color = #3B82F6
semantic color.surface: Color = color.primitive.blue.500
background = color.surface @ opacity.surface.tint
```

### `Opacity`

An alpha multiplier in 0…1. Name it so themes can remap scrims and tints. A bare Opacity token is not a layer — apply it with `color @ opacity` or an `opacity:` argument.

Category: alpha. Used on: [`opacity`](#opacity), `color @ …`, [`GradientStop`](#gradientstop).[`opacity`](#opacity), [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer).[`opacity`](#opacity).

Accepted syntax:

- `0.4` — [`Number`](#number) in 0…1. Fine for a primitive; avoid raw decimals on library surfaces.
- `opacity.token` — An Opacity token. Preferred on the right of `@` and on `opacity=`.

```pdl
primitive opacity.primitive.scrim: Opacity = 0.4
semantic opacity.surface.tint: Opacity = opacity.primitive.scrim
foreground = color.ink @ opacity.surface.tint
```

### `Distance`

A non-negative length in design units (pixels in the HTML preview). Used for gaps and inset axes. Not a string; there is no `px` suffix.

Category: spacing. Used on: `gap`, `columnGap`, `rowGap`, `EdgeInsets axes`.

Accepted syntax:

- `12` — Non-negative number.
- `space.stack` — A Distance token (semantic alias of a primitive).

Rejected:

- `12px` — No unit suffix.
- `-4` — Negative lengths are rejected.

```pdl
primitive spacing.primitive.md: Distance = 12
semantic space.stack: Distance = spacing.primitive.md
gap = space.stack
```

### `Radius`

A uniform corner radius (or a blur radius amount). A number. Per-corner values are [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii) via [`Corner(…)`](#corner), which is not a Radius token RHS.

Category: shape. Used on: `cornerRadius`, [`Blur`](#blur).[`radius`](#radius).

Accepted syntax:

- `10` — Non-negative number.
- `radius.md` — A Radius token.

Rejected:

- `Corner(tl: 8, tr: 8, br: 4, bl: 4)` — That produces [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii), not Radius. PDL-E005 on a Radius token.

```pdl
primitive radius.primitive.md: Radius = 10
semantic radius.card: Radius = radius.primitive.md
cornerRadius = radius.card
```

### `Shadow`

A drop shadow. Axes are numbers (or numeric tokens); color is a [`Color`](#color). Optional spread defaults to 0. HTML preview maps the resolved object to CSS box-shadow.

Category: effect. Used on: [`shadow`](#shadow).

Accepted syntax:

- `Shadow(x:, y:, blurRadius:, color:)` — Required fields. color may be hex, a [`Color`](#color) token, or `color @ opacity`.
- `Shadow(…, spread: 0)` — Optional spread; omit for 0.
- `shadow.card` — A Shadow token.

Rejected:

- `"0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.15)"` — A CSS box-shadow string is PDL-E005.

```pdl
primitive shadow.card: Shadow = Shadow(x: 0, y: 4, blurRadius: 12, color: #000000 @ 0.15)
shadow = shadow.card
```

### `Icon`

A tintable glyph reference. This is the value of an icon frame’s `icon:` property — not the Icon() frame constructor.

Category: asset. Used on: [`icon`](#icon-frame).[`icon`](#icon-frame).

Accepted syntax:

- `IconRef(system: .sfSymbols, name: "star")` — SF Symbol. System is [`IconSystem`](#iconsystem).
- `IconRef(system: .materialSymbols, name: "star")` — Material Symbol.
- `IconRef(file: "icons/star.svg")` — Pack-relative file. No leading /.
- `"icons/star.svg"` — Path sugar: must contain `/` and/or a known extension.
- `icon.action.favorite` — An Icon token.

Rejected:

- `"star"` — Bare glyph id is ambiguous — PDL-E005.
- `Icon(icon: …)` — That builds an icon frame, not an Icon token.

```pdl
primitive icon.primitive.star: Icon = IconRef(system: .sfSymbols, name: "star")
semantic icon.action.favorite: Icon = icon.primitive.star
icon = icon.action.favorite
```

### `MediaSource`

Where a raster, vector, or video comes from. Distinct from the Media() frame and from MediaLayer (a fill).

Category: asset. Used on: [`media`](#media-frame).`source`, [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer).`source`.

Accepted syntax:

- `MediaSource(file: "media/hero.jpg")` — Pack-relative file. No leading /. Kind/format inferred from a known extension when omitted.
- `MediaSource(url: "https://…")` — Remote http(s) URL.
- `MediaSource(url: "https://…", kind: .raster, format: .jpeg)` — Opaque CDN address: set kind (and format when known). Kind and format must agree (PDL-E006).
- `"media/hero.jpg"` — Path-string sugar.
- `"https://cdn.example/hero.jpg"` — URL-string sugar.
- `media.hero` — A MediaSource token.

```pdl
primitive media.hero: MediaSource = MediaSource(url: "https://cdn.example/abc", kind: .raster, format: .jpeg)
source = media.hero
```

### `Ratio`

A positive width/height ratio.

Category: layout. Used on: [`Sizing`](#sizing).`aspect`, `aspect`.

Accepted syntax:

- `1.777` — Positive number (width ÷ height).
- `16:9` — W:H sugar; same as 16/9.
- `ratio.video` — A Ratio token.

```pdl
primitive ratio.video: Ratio = 16:9
width = .aspect(ratio.video)
```

### `FontFamily`

A font stack. Quoted string.

Category: typography. Used on: [`fontFamily`](#fontfamily), [`typeStyle`](#typestyle).[`fontFamily`](#fontfamily).

Accepted syntax:

- `"Inter, system-ui, sans-serif"` — CSS-style stack.
- `font.body` — A FontFamily token.

```pdl
primitive font.body: FontFamily = "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif"
fontFamily = font.body
```

### `Size`

Font size or icon box size in design units. Unitless — not `16px`.

Category: typography. Used on: `fontSize`, [`icon`](#icon-frame).[`size`](#size).

Accepted syntax:

- `16` — [`Number`](#number).
- `type.size.body` — A Size token.

```pdl
primitive type.size.body: Size = 16
fontSize = type.size.body
```

### `Weight`

Font weight as a number (400, 500, 600, …).

Category: typography. Used on: `fontWeight`.

Accepted syntax:

- `500` — Numeric weight.
- `type.weight.medium` — A Weight token.

```pdl
primitive type.weight.medium: Weight = 500
fontWeight = type.weight.medium
```

### `LineHeight`

Leading as a unitless ratio of fontSize. 1.35 means 135%. Must be greater than 0.

Category: typography. Used on: [`lineHeight`](#lineheight).

Accepted syntax:

- `1.35` — Positive number.
- `type.lineHeight.body` — A LineHeight token.

```pdl
primitive type.lineHeight.body: LineHeight = 1.35
lineHeight = type.lineHeight.body
```

### `LetterSpacing`

Tracking in em — a fraction of fontSize. May be negative.

Category: typography. Used on: [`letterSpacing`](#letterspacing).

Accepted syntax:

- `-0.01` — [`Number`](#number) in em.
- `type.letterSpacing.tight` — A LetterSpacing token.

```pdl
primitive type.letterSpacing.tight: LetterSpacing = -0.01
letterSpacing = type.letterSpacing.tight
```

### `Sizing`

How a width or height is computed. Write `.hug` or `Sizing.hug`. A bare number on a sizing property means `.fixed(n)`. Rare as a token; usual on frames.

Category: layout. Used on: `width`, `height`.

Accepted syntax:

- `.hug` — [`Size`](#size) to content.
- `.fill` — Fill the parent on that axis.
- `.fixed(n)` — Exactly n design units.
- `240` — On width/height, the same as `.fixed(240)`.
- `.flex(min:, preferred:, max:)` — Flexible range. Any field may be omitted. All omitted is like [`.fill`](#contentmode). preferred maps to flex-basis (or the host equivalent).
- `.aspect(r)` — Derive this axis from the other so width/height = r. r is a number, W:H, or a [`Ratio`](#ratio) token. Put .aspect on the free axis only.
- `sizing.sidebar` — A Sizing token.

```pdl
primitive sizing.sidebar: Sizing = .fill
width = .fill
height = .hug
width = 240
```

### `Duration`

Draft. Animation length in milliseconds. Unitless — not `150ms`.

Category: motion (draft). Used on: [`Transition`](#transition).[`duration`](#duration), `animate`.

Accepted syntax:

- `150` — Milliseconds.
- `motion.duration.fast` — A Duration token.

```pdl
primitive motion.duration.fast: Duration = 150
primitive motion.duration.standard: Duration = 250
```

### `Easing`

Draft. A timing curve. A quoted CSS easing string.

Category: motion (draft). Used on: [`Transition`](#transition).[`easing`](#easing).

Accepted syntax:

- `"linear"` — Linear curve.
- `"cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)"` — Cubic bezier.
- `motion.easing.standard` — An Easing token.

```pdl
primitive motion.easing.standard: Easing = "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)"
primitive motion.easing.linear: Easing = "linear"
```

### `Transition`

Draft. A duration plus easing, and an optional delay (default 0). Written as a tuple, not a constructor call. Themes replace a Transition wholly — no deep merge.

Category: motion (draft). Used on: `animate`.

Accepted syntax:

- `(duration: …, easing: …)` — Required fields. Values may be literals or [`Duration`](#duration) / [`Easing`](#easing) tokens.
- `(duration: …, easing: …, delay: …)` — Optional delay in milliseconds.
- `motion.appear` — A Transition token.

```pdl
semantic motion.appear: Transition = (duration: motion.duration.standard, easing: motion.easing.standard)
semantic motion.instant: Transition = (duration: 0, easing: motion.easing.linear)
```

### `Blur`

A blur layer object. [`Radius`](#radius) amounts reuse [`Radius`](#radius) — there is no numeric Blur token. A bare Blur token is a valid layer entry. Legacy `Blur(blur: …)` is rejected.

Category: layer. Used on: [`background`](#background), [`foreground`](#foreground).

Accepted syntax:

- `Blur(radius: 16)` — [`Radius`](#radius) is a number or [`Radius`](#radius) token.
- `Blur(radius: …, style: .standard)` — Optional [`BlurStyle`](#blurstyle). v1 ships only [`.standard`](#blurstyle).
- `Blur(radius: …, vibrancy: Vibrancy(…))` — Optional [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy).
- `blur.sheet` — A Blur token; legal inside a layer list.

Rejected:

- `16` — A bare number is a [`Radius`](#radius), not a Blur.
- `Blur(blur: 16)` — Legacy argument name — rejected.

```pdl
primitive blur.sheet.radius: Radius = 16
primitive blur.sheet: Blur = Blur(radius: blur.sheet.radius)
background = [blur.sheet, color.surface]
```

### `Vibrancy`

Saturation and brightness for a blur (or as its own layer token).

Category: layer. Used on: [`Blur`](#blur).[`vibrancy`](#vibrancy), [`background`](#background), [`foreground`](#foreground).

Accepted syntax:

- `Vibrancy(saturation:, brightness:)` — Both fields are numbers.
- `vibrancy.sheet` — A Vibrancy token; legal as a layer entry.

```pdl
primitive vibrancy.sheet: Vibrancy = Vibrancy(saturation: 1.2, brightness: 1.05)
primitive blur.sheet: Blur = Blur(radius: 16, vibrancy: vibrancy.sheet)
```

### `Ramp`

An opacity or color ramp along an axis. [`Direction`](#direction) is [`RampDirection`](#rampdirection). Stops are [`GradientStop`](#gradientstop) values.

Category: layer. Used on: [`background`](#background), [`foreground`](#foreground).

Accepted syntax:

- `Ramp(direction:, stops: […])` — Preferred constructor.
- `(direction:, stops: […])` — Naked tuple; still accepted.
- `ramp.fade.bottom` — A Ramp token.

```pdl
primitive ramp.fade.bottom: Ramp = Ramp(
  direction: .bottomToTop,
  stops: [
    GradientStop(opacity: 1, position: 0.5),
    GradientStop(opacity: 0, position: 1)
  ]
)
```

### `EdgeInsets`

A box inset. Axes may be numbers or [`Distance`](#distance) tokens. A bare number on padding, margin, or inset means uniform insets on all four sides. That sugar does not apply to gap.

Category: layout. Used on: `padding`, `margin`, `inset`.

Accepted syntax:

- `EdgeInsets(x:, y:)` — Horizontal and vertical pairs.
- `EdgeInsets(top:, right:, bottom:, left:)` — Per-side.
- `16` — On padding / margin / inset only: uniform EdgeInsets.
- `spacing.card.pad` — An EdgeInsets token.

```pdl
primitive spacing.card.pad: EdgeInsets = EdgeInsets(x: 16, y: 12)
padding = spacing.card.pad
padding = 16
margin = EdgeInsets(top: 8, right: 12, bottom: 8, left: 12)
```

### `CornerRadii`

Per-corner radii. The type name is CornerRadii; the constructor name is [`Corner`](#corner). Axes are numbers or [`Radius`](#radius) tokens. A [`Radius`](#radius) token stays uniform — do not assign Corner(…) to a [`Radius`](#radius) token.

Category: shape. Used on: `cornerRadius`.

Accepted syntax:

- `Corner(tl:, tr:, br:, bl:)` — Asymmetric radii on a frame’s cornerRadius.
- `10` — On cornerRadius, a number is a uniform [`Radius`](#radius), not CornerRadii.

```pdl
let corners: CornerRadii = Corner(tl: 8, tr: 8, br: 4, bl: 4)
cornerRadius = corners
cornerRadius = Corner(tl: radius.md, tr: radius.md, br: radius.sm, bl: radius.sm)
```

### `Media`

A media fill inside a background or foreground stack. Construct with [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer). Not the Media() frame, and not a MediaSource (that is the address).

Category: layer. Used on: [`background`](#background), [`foreground`](#foreground).

Accepted syntax:

- `MediaLayer(source:, contentMode: …)` — source is a [`MediaSource`](#mediasource); contentMode is [`ContentMode`](#contentmode). Optional opacity:.
- `heroFill` — A Media (layer) token or value-let.

Rejected:

- `Media(source: …)` — That builds a media frame, not a layer fill.
- `MediaLayer(…) @ 0.5` — Do not postfix @ if opacity: is already set (PDL-E020).

```pdl
let hero: Media = MediaLayer(source: media.hero, contentMode: .cover)
background = [hero, color.surface]
```

### `GradientStop`

One stop in a [`Ramp`](#ramp). [`Position`](#position) is 0…1. Supply opacity, color, or both.

Category: layer. Used on: [`Ramp`](#ramp).`stops`.

Accepted syntax:

- `GradientStop(position:, opacity:)` — Fade stop.
- `GradientStop(position:, color:)` — [`Color`](#color) stop.
- `GradientStop(position:, opacity:, color:)` — Both.

```pdl
let fadeOut: GradientStop = GradientStop(opacity: 0, position: 1)
stops = [GradientStop(opacity: 1, position: 0), fadeOut]
```

### `Background`

A named layer stack composited under children. Same right-hand side as [`Foreground`](#foreground): a color, or an ordered list of layers. Prefer `color @ opacityToken` over raw decimals. A bare [`Opacity`](#opacity) token is not a layer.

Category: layer. Used on: [`background`](#background).

Accepted syntax:

- `color.surface` — Scalar color sugar — one solid layer.
- `[blur.sheet, color.surface @ opacity.tint]` — Ordered layers, bottom first.
- `material.sheet` — A Background token.

```pdl
semantic material.sheet: Background = [blur.sheet, color.surface @ opacity.surface.tint]
background = material.sheet
```

### `Foreground`

A named layer stack composited over children. Same right-hand side as [`Background`](#background).

Category: layer. Used on: [`foreground`](#foreground).

Accepted syntax:

- `color.ink @ opacity.state.hover` — Scalar color sugar.
- `[color.ink @ opacity.state.hover]` — Layer list.
- `effect.hoverTint` — A Foreground token.

```pdl
semantic effect.hoverTint: Foreground = [color.ink @ opacity.state.hover]
foreground = effect.hoverTint
```

## Theme {#theme}

A named remap of tokens you already declared. Use a theme for light/dark, brand, or reduced motion. Components keep using semantic names; the theme changes what those names resolve to.

A named override bundle. Each line is `tokenName = value`. The left side is a declared `primitive` or `semantic` (prefer semantics so components stay stable). The right side is a value of that token’s type — another token, or a literal. The assignment replaces the whole token; there is no field-by-field merge inside a [`Shadow`](#shadow) or [`Transition`](#transition). Themes do not inherit. Write one theme per concern (Dark, ReducedMotion) and combine them when you bake or in the Playground — not with `theme Child: Parent`.

Accepted syntax:

- `theme Name { … }` — Declare a named bundle. Name is an identifier, not a string.
- `color.surface = color.ink` — Remap a semantic to another token. Preferred.
- `color.surface = #111827` — Literal of the token’s type. Fine for a skin; prefer a token ref when the value is reused.
- `motion.appear = motion.instant` — Replace a structured token wholly ([`Transition`](#transition), [`Shadow`](#shadow), [`Background`](#background), …).

Rejected:

- `theme Dark: Light { … }` — Do not author parent/child themes. The `:` form is parsed but is not how themes combine.
- `shadow.card.x = 2` — No dotted field patch. Assign a new Shadow(…) to [`shadow.card`](#shadow).

```pdl
primitive color.white: Color = #FFFFFF
primitive color.ink: Color = #111827
semantic color.surface: Color = color.white
semantic color.text: Color = color.ink

theme Dark {
  color.surface = color.ink
  color.text = color.white
}
```

## typeStyle {#typestyle}

A named bundle of text-frame properties. A text frame sets `style = Name`. Body lines are the same properties as a text frame.

A named bundle of text-frame properties. Each line is `name = value` using the same property names as a text frame ([`fontFamily`](#fontfamily), `fontSize`, `fontWeight`, [`lineHeight`](#lineheight), [`letterSpacing`](#letterspacing), …). A text frame applies the bundle with `style = Name`. Later frame props win over the style. `style = null` clears the binding.

Accepted syntax:

- `typeStyle Body { fontSize = 16 … }` — Declare a named bundle. Body is text-frame props only.
- `style = Body` — Apply the bundle on a text frame (constructor arg or assignment).
- `style = null` — Clear the type-style binding without inventing typography literals.

Rejected:

- `typeStyle Card { direction = .row }` — [`Layout`](#layout) props are not text-frame props.

```pdl
typeStyle Heading {
  fontFamily = "Inter"
  fontSize = 24
  fontWeight = 700
  lineHeight = 1.35
}

component TypographyShowcase() layout {
  direction = .column
  gap = 8
  let heading = Text(content: "Heading style sample", style: Heading)
  children = [heading]
}
```

## Values {#values}

Structured values you pass to properties — insets, shadows, corners, gradient stops.

### Corner {#corner}

Asymmetric radii: Corner(tl:, tr:, br:, bl:). Produces [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii). A number on cornerRadius is a uniform [`Radius`](#radius).

| Constructor | Meaning |
|-------------|--------|
| [`EdgeInsets(…)`](#edgeinsets) | Box inset. EdgeInsets(x:, y:) or EdgeInsets(top:, right:, bottom:, left:). A number on padding/margin/inset means uniform [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets). |
| [`Corner(…)`](#corner) | Asymmetric radii: Corner(tl:, tr:, br:, bl:). Produces [`CornerRadii`](#cornerradii). A number on cornerRadius is a uniform [`Radius`](#radius). |
| [`Shadow(…)`](#shadow) | Shadow(x:, y:, blurRadius:, color: [, spread:]). Axes are numbers or numeric tokens; color is a [`Color`](#color). spread defaults to 0. |
| [`GradientStop(…)`](#gradientstop) | GradientStop(position: 0…1 [, opacity:] [, color:]). |
| [`Vibrancy(…)`](#vibrancy) | Vibrancy(saturation:, brightness:). Used on [`Blur`](#blur) or as its own layer token. |

## Layers {#layers}

Fills stacked in [`background`](#background) and [`foreground`](#foreground). A hex [`Color`](#color) is usually enough; use these constructors for a gradient, blur, or a [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer).

### MediaLayer {#medialayer}

[`Media`](#media) fill in a background/foreground stack: MediaLayer(source:, contentMode: … [, opacity:]). Produces token type [`Media`](#media). Do not postfix @ if opacity: is already set (PDL-E020).

| Constructor | Meaning |
|-------------|--------|
| [`Color(…)`](#color) | Layer constructor Color(color: …). The token type [`Color`](#color) is the same name — a hex or token is usually enough; use Color(…) inside a layer list when you need the explicit form. |
| [`Ramp(…)`](#ramp) | Ramp(direction: [`RampDirection`](#rampdirection), stops: [GradientStop, …]). Also a token type. |
| [`Blur(…)`](#blur) | Blur(radius: [, style: [`BlurStyle`](#blurstyle)] [, vibrancy: [`Vibrancy`](#vibrancy)]). Not a bare number. Legacy Blur(blur: …) is rejected. |
| [`MediaLayer(…)`](#medialayer) | [`Media`](#media) fill in a background/foreground stack: MediaLayer(source:, contentMode: … [, opacity:]). Produces token type [`Media`](#media). Do not postfix @ if opacity: is already set (PDL-E020). |

## Assets {#assets}

How you point at a glyph or a file. [`IconRef`](#iconref) is the [`Icon`](#icon) token RHS; [`MediaSource`](#mediasource) is the source for a [`media`](#media-frame) frame and [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer).

### IconRef {#iconref}

Concrete glyph: `IconRef(system: IconSystem, name: "…")` or `IconRef(file: "icons/…")`. This is the [`Icon`](#icon) token RHS — not the [`Icon()`](#icon-frame) frame.

| Constructor | Meaning |
|-------------|--------|
| [`IconRef(…)`](#iconref) | Concrete glyph: `IconRef(system: IconSystem, name: "…")` or `IconRef(file: "icons/…")`. This is the [`Icon`](#icon) token RHS — not the [`Icon()`](#icon-frame) frame. |
| [`MediaSource(…)`](#mediasource) | MediaSource(file: "…" [, kind:] [, format:]) or MediaSource(url: "…" [, kind:] [, format:]). Pack paths have no leading /. |

## Enums

Closed choices such as [`.row`](#direction) or `.center`. Use them on layout properties and as parameter types.

### `Direction`

Main axis of a layout (or overlap mode for stack).

Used on: [`layout`](#layout).[`direction`](#direction).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.row` | Main axis left to right. |
| `.column` | Main axis top to bottom. |
| `.rowReverse` | Main axis right to left. |
| `.columnReverse` | Main axis bottom to top. |
| `.stack` | Children share one box. Array order is painter’s order: first at the back, last on top. |
| `.reverseStack` | Same overlap as stack; first child is on top. |

```pdl
component Stack() layout {
  direction = .column
  gap = 8
  let title = Text(content: "Hello")
  let body = Text(content: "World")
  children = [title, body]
}
```

### `Wrap`

Whether children wrap to another line on the main axis.

Used on: [`layout`](#layout).[`wrap`](#wrap).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.nowrap` | Keep children on one line (default). |
| `.wrap` | Wrap onto additional lines. rowGap / columnGap apply. |

```pdl
direction = .row
wrap = .wrap
columnGap = 8
rowGap = 8
```

### `Align`

Cross-axis alignment in a layout; vertical placement of text or media content in its box.

Used on: [`layout`](#layout).[`align`](#align), [`text`](#text).[`align`](#align), [`media`](#media-frame).[`align`](#align).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.start` | Toward the start of the cross axis (top in a row; left in a column). On text/media: top of the box. |
| `.center` | Centered on the cross axis (or vertically in a text/media box). |
| `.end` | Toward the end of the cross axis. On text/media: bottom of the box. |
| `.stretch` | Stretch on the cross axis. [`Layout`](#layout) only — illegal on text and media (PDL-E006). |

```pdl
direction = .row
align = .center
let caption = Text(content: "Hi", align: .start)
```

### `Justify`

Main-axis distribution in a layout; horizontal placement of text or media content in its box.

Used on: [`layout`](#layout).[`justify`](#justify), [`text`](#text).[`justify`](#justify), [`media`](#media-frame).[`justify`](#justify).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.start` | Pack toward the start of the main axis. On text/media: left of the box. |
| `.center` | Centered on the main axis (or horizontally in a text/media box). |
| `.end` | Pack toward the end. On text/media: right of the box. |
| `.stretch` | Stretch along the main axis. [`Layout`](#layout) only — illegal on text and media (PDL-E006). |
| `.spaceBetween` | First and last flush to the ends; even space between. [`Layout`](#layout) only. |
| `.spaceAround` | Even space around each child. [`Layout`](#layout) only. |

```pdl
direction = .row
width = .fill
justify = .spaceBetween
```

### `Overflow`

What happens when content does not fit the frame. There is no .hidden or [`.auto`](#alignself).

Used on: [`layout`](#layout).[`overflow`](#overflow), [`text`](#text).[`overflow`](#overflow).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.visible` | Content may paint outside the box. |
| `.scroll` | Content clips and the host may scroll. |
| `.clip` | Content is clipped; no scroll. Use this instead of CSS overflow:hidden. |

```pdl
width = 200
height = 80
overflow = .clip
```

### `BorderPosition`

Where the stroke is painted. Borders never change the layout box size.

Used on: [`layout`](#layout).[`borderPosition`](#borderposition), [`text`](#text).[`borderPosition`](#borderposition).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.outside` | Stroke outside the border box (default when omitted). |
| `.inside` | Stroke inside the border box. |

```pdl
borderWidth = 1
borderColor = #111111
borderPosition = .inside
```

### `TruncateStyle`

How leftover text is cut when lineClamp is set.

Used on: [`text`](#text).[`truncateStyle`](#truncatestyle).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.clip` | Hard cut after N lines; no ellipsis. |
| `.ellipsis` | Trailing … after the last painted line. Default if lineClamp is set and truncateStyle is omitted. |

```pdl
let blurb = Text(content: longCopy, lineClamp: 2, truncateStyle: .ellipsis)
```

### `ContentMode`

How a media source fits its box.

Used on: [`media`](#media-frame).[`contentMode`](#contentmode), [`MediaLayer`](#medialayer).[`contentMode`](#contentmode).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.cover` | Fill the box; crop overflow. Preserves aspect ratio. |
| `.contain` | Fit entirely inside the box; may letterbox. |
| `.fill` | Stretch to the box; may distort. |
| `.scaleDown` | Like contain, but never scale up above intrinsic size. |

```pdl
let hero = Media(source: media.hero, contentMode: .cover, width: .fill, height: 160)
```

### `AlignSelf`

Override the parent’s align for this child only.

Used on: `child`.[`alignSelf`](#alignself).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.start` | Cross-axis start, ignoring parent align. |
| `.center` | Cross-axis center. |
| `.end` | Cross-axis end. |
| `.stretch` | Stretch on the cross axis. |
| `.auto` | Use the parent’s align (default). |

```pdl
direction = .row
align = .start
let sidebar = Layout(width: 200, alignSelf: .stretch, children: [])
children = [sidebar, body]
```

### `Position`

Whether a child of a layout sits in the flex flow. Set `position` and `inset` on the **child** (constructor args or `Child.position = …`), not on the parent. There is no `x` / `y` / `top =` property. Placement is only `position` + `inset`. `inset` is [`EdgeInsets`](#edgeinsets) from the parent’s **padding box**. The child must still appear in [`children`](#children) — `.absolute` does not mount it.

Used on: `child`.[`position`](#position), `child`.`inset`.

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.flow` | In-flow flex child (default). `inset` is ignored. |
| `.absolute` | Out of flow. Pin with `inset`. `inset = 8` is 8 on all four sides; `EdgeInsets(top:, right:, bottom:, left:)` parks a corner (use 0 on the sides you do not pin). |

```pdl
let body = Text(content: "Card")
let badge = Text(
  content: "New",
  position: .absolute,
  inset: EdgeInsets(top: 8, right: 8, bottom: 0, left: 0)
)
children = [body, badge]
```

### `BlurStyle`

Which blur the preview uses. v1 only has `.standard`.

Used on: [`Blur`](#blur).`style`.

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.standard` | Default host blur. The only v1 case. |

```pdl
background = [Blur(radius: 16, style: .standard), color.surface]
```

### `RampDirection`

Axis of a Ramp (gradient / opacity mask). Not a frame-prop enum — only on [`Ramp`](#ramp).

Used on: [`Ramp`](#ramp).[`direction`](#direction).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.topToBottom` | Linear; start at the top edge. |
| `.bottomToTop` | Linear; start at the bottom edge. |
| `.leftToRight` | Linear; start at the left edge. |
| `.rightToLeft` | Linear; start at the right edge. |
| `.radial` | From the center. [`GradientStop.position`](#gradientstop) is a fraction of radius (0 = center, 1 = edge). |

```pdl
background = Ramp(
  direction: .bottomToTop,
  stops: [
    GradientStop(opacity: 1, position: 0),
    GradientStop(opacity: 0, position: 1)
  ]
)
```

### `IconSystem`

Which symbol library an [`IconRef`](#iconref) names.

Used on: [`IconRef`](#iconref).`system`.

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.sfSymbols` | SF Symbols (Apple). |
| `.materialSymbols` | Material Symbols. |

```pdl
icon = IconRef(system: .sfSymbols, name: "star")
```

### `MediaKind`

Role of a media address when the extension is missing or ambiguous.

Used on: [`MediaSource`](#mediasource).`kind`.

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.raster` | Bitmap (JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, …). |
| `.vector` | SVG / PDF / design vector. |
| `.video` | Video file or stream. |

```pdl
primitive media.hero: MediaSource = MediaSource(url: "https://cdn.example/abc", kind: .raster)
```

### `MediaFormat`

Closed file format. Must agree with kind when both are set (PDL-E006). .jpg is an alias of .jpeg.

Used on: [`MediaSource`](#mediasource).`format`.

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.webp` | WebP image. |
| `.jpeg` | JPEG image (.jpg is the same case). |
| `.png` | PNG image. |
| `.gif` | GIF image. |
| `.svg` | SVG vector. |
| `.mp4` | MP4 video. |
| `.webm` | WebM video. |
| `.pdf` | PDF page / vector. |

```pdl
primitive media.hero: MediaSource = MediaSource(url: "https://cdn.example/abc", kind: .raster, format: .jpeg)
```

### `RuleStrength`

How seriously a failed [`Rule`](#rule) is treated — stop the build, or just warn.

Used on: [`Rule`](#rule).

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.must` | Violation is an error (fails validation / CI). |
| `.mustNot` | If the query matches, error. |
| `.should` | Violation is a warning. |
| `.shouldNot` | If the query matches, warning. |

```pdl
rules TabBar {
  tags = ["tab-bar"]
  Rule(.must, children.where(tag: "tab-item").count.between(2, 5),
    description: "A tab bar has between 2 and 5 tabs.")
}
```

## Messages {#messages}

A component hears its parameters. That is enough for a fixture, and for a parent that already knows the state. It is not enough when the user clicks a chip, or when a field should start editing. PDL does not run like a script in the page. The host — the preview, or the app that embeds the design — delivers pointer and text events onto a component that opted in (`<PointerInput>`, `<EditableText>`). The component can then emit a typed channel to its parent (`select`, `change`). The parent assigns on that channel and its own parameters update, so the row can show which chip is selected. A component can also ask the host to do something, such as begin editing. Those are three different paths. A `pressEnd` is not an emit.

| Surface | Direction | Author wires with | Meaning |
|---------|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| `emits` | Child → parent | `emit select(filter)` in a host handler; parent writes `item.select(…) = { … }` | The child tells the parent something happened (selected, changed). |
| `host inbound` | Environment → component | `self.pressEnd = { … }` in the component body (self. is optional) | The preview tells the component the user hovered, clicked, or typed. Opt in with `<PointerInput>` or `<EditableText>`. |
| `host verbs` | Component → environment | `beginEditing(value)` inside a handler | The component asks the preview to do something — start or end typing. |

```pdl
component Chip <PointerInput>(title: String = "All") layout {
  let label = Text(content: title)
  children = [label]
  self.pressEnd = { emit select(title) }
} emits {
  select(title: String)
}
```

## Emits

How a child tells its parent something happened — a chip was selected, a field changed. Declare the channel, fire it from a click, and listen on the parent.

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `emits C { select(filter: FilterId) }` | Declare what this component can tell its parent, in a separate block. Each field needs a type. |
| `} emits { select(filter: FilterId) }` | The same channels, written right after the component body. |
| `protocol P: component { emits { select(filter: FilterId) } }` | One shared channel for every component that follows the protocol — a mixed list of chips all `select`. |
| `emit select(filter)` | Fire the channel from a click (or other host handler). Pass values that match the declared types. |
| `emit open(self)` | Send this whole instance to the parent — “open this row.” |
| `all.select(filter_id: FilterId) = { … }` | The parent hears one named child (`All`) and updates its own state. |
| `chip.select(filter_id: FilterId) = { … }` | The parent hears each item in a list. Write this on `chip`, not on `chips`. |

```pdl
enum FilterId {
  case all
  case podcasts
}

component FilterChip <PointerInput>(
  title: String = "All",
  filter: FilterId = .all,
  selected: Bool = false
) layout {
  let label = Text(content: title)
  children = [label]
  self.pressEnd = { emit select(filter) }
} emits {
  select(filter: FilterId)
}

component FilterBar(currentFilter: FilterId = .all) layout {
  let all = FilterChip(title: "All", filter: .all, selected: currentFilter == .all)
  let podcasts = FilterChip(title: "Podcasts", filter: .podcasts, selected: currentFilter == .podcasts)
  children = [all, podcasts]
  all.select(filter_id: FilterId) = { currentFilter = filter_id }
  podcasts.select(filter_id: FilterId) = { currentFilter = filter_id }
}
```

## Protocols

A shared contract so several components can sit in the same list and speak the same language. Use an API protocol when different chip types all `select`. Use a host protocol when the preview must deliver clicks or typing.

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `protocol P: component { … }` | A contract for components that share parameters and emits. Use for mixed lists and slots. |
| `protocol P { host … }` | A contract with the preview — clicks, editing. Not something you put in a list. |
| `component C <P>(…) kind { … }` | This component follows protocol P. It gets P’s parameters and may use P’s host events. |
| `requires PointerInput` | This API protocol also needs preview events (clicks or typing). |
| `title = ""` | A parameter every conforming component has. |

```pdl
protocol SubnavItem: component {
  requires PointerInput
  title = ""
  filter: FilterId = .all
  emits { select(filter: FilterId) }
}

component FilterChip <SubnavItem>(
  selected: Bool = false
) layout {
  let label = Text(content: title)
  children = [label]
  self.pressEnd = { emit select(filter) }
}

component LibrarySubnav(
  currentFilter: FilterId = .all,
  chips: [SubnavItem] = [
    FilterChip(title: "All", filter: .all),
    FilterChip(title: "Podcasts", filter: .podcasts)
  ]
) layout {
  ForEach(chips) { chip in
    chip.selected = self.currentFilter == filter
    chip.select(filter_id: FilterId) = { currentFilter = filter_id }
  }
  children = chips
}
```

## Host Protocols {#host-protocols}

A host protocol lets the preview (or app) trigger component changes: hover color, a click, focus, typing. Use [`PointerInput`](#pointerinput) for buttons and chips; use [`EditableText`](#editabletext) for a field the user types into. Opt in with `component C <PointerInput>`. These names are built in — you do not import them.

### `PointerInput`

Use this when a component should react to hover, click, focus, or appear/dismiss — a button that changes color on hover, a chip that selects on click. Write `component Chip <PointerInput>` then `self.pressEnd = { … }`.

Events from the preview:

| Channel | Meaning |
|---------|--------|
| `hoverStart` | Pointer entered the component. |
| `hoverEnd` | Pointer left the component. |
| `pressStart` | Pointer or button went down. |
| `pressEnd` | Pointer or button went up — the usual tap / click complete. |
| `pressCancel` | The press was aborted (drag-off or system cancel). |
| `focusStart` | Keyboard or accessibility focus entered. |
| `focusEnd` | Focus left. |
| `activate` | Primary activation (Enter / accessibility activate), distinct from press. |
| `appear` | The component became visible / entered the tree. |
| `dismiss` | The host asked this component to dismiss (sheet, modal). |

```pdl
component Chip <PointerInput>(title: String = "All") layout {
  let label = Text(content: title)
  children = [label]
  self.pressEnd = { emit select(title) }
} emits {
  select(title: String)
}
```

### `EditableText`

Use this for a field the user can type into. Pair with kind [`text`](#text). The preview starts editing on click or focus by default. Show the typed string with `content = self.value`.

Events from the preview:

| Channel | Meaning |
|---------|--------|
| `editingBegan` | The editing session started. |
| `editingFinished` | The session committed. Keep `value`. |
| `editingCancelled` | The session aborted. Restore the checkpoint. |
| `keyboardDismissed` | Older name for `editingFinished`. |
| `keyboardCancelled` | Older name for `editingCancelled`. |

Calls you make to the preview:

| Verb | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `beginEditing(startingValue)` | Start a session seeded with this string. |
| `finishEditing()` | Commit the session. |
| `cancelEditing()` | Abort the session and restore the checkpoint. |
| `commitEditing()` | Older name for `finishEditing()`. |

State the preview adds to the component:

| Name | Type | Meaning |
|------|------|--------|
| `value` | [`String`](#string) | What the user has typed. Default "". |
| `isEditing` | [`Bool`](#bool) | True while the field is being edited. |
| `isEmpty` | [`Bool`](#bool) | True when `value` is empty. |
| `isOverLimit` | [`Bool`](#bool) | True when `value` is longer than the host limit. |
| `activatesOn` | [`TextFieldActivation`](#textfieldactivation) | When editing starts. Default [`.focus`](#textfieldactivation). |

#### `TextFieldActivation` {#textfieldactivation}

When a text field starts editing. Use `.focus` for the usual click-or-focus field; `.none` if only your code should start editing.

Used on: `activatesOn`.

| Case | Meaning |
|------|--------|
| `.focus` | Default. Click, tap, or focus begins editing. |
| `.press` | Begin on press/click only — not bare focus. |
| `.none` | Program-only. Call beginEditing yourself; the leaf hit-test does not begin. |

```pdl
component Note <EditableText>() text {
  content = self.value
  activatesOn = .none
}
```

```pdl
component SearchField <EditableText>(
  placeholder: String = "Search"
) text {
  content = placeholder
  if isEditing {
    content = self.value
  } else if !isEmpty {
    content = self.value
  }
  self.editingFinished = {
    finishEditing()
    emit change(value)
  }
} emits {
  change(value: String)
}
```

## Handler motion (draft) {#motion}

Animation clauses on host handlers: which [`Transition`](#transition) to run, enter/exit snapshots, and list stagger. Bake stays at rest pose; the HTML host plays a CSS overlay.

Host handler bodies may name a [`Transition`](#transition) and enter/exit snapshots. Bake is the rest pose. The HTML host plays a CSS overlay — not layout. Units: [`Duration`](#duration) is milliseconds; translate and blur are CSS pixels; scale is unitless; opacity is 0…1. v1 props: [`opacity`](#opacity), `scale`, `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `translateX`, `translateY`, [`blur`](#blur). Unknown keys in `from` / `to` are ignored. `animate = motion.appear` selects a [`Transition`](#transition) token or tuple. `from { … }` is the appear start snapshot; `to { … }` is the dismiss end snapshot. `stagger` is a millisecond increment between direct visible child frames; `staggerFrom` is `.first` or `.last`.

Accepted syntax:

- `animate = motion.interactive` — Use this [`Transition`](#transition) for property changes this handler triggers (implicit interpolation) and for from/to snapshots.
- `from { opacity = 0 scale = 0.95 translateY = 8 }` — Enter snapshot on `appear`. translateY is px; scale is unitless.
- `to { opacity = 0 }` — Exit snapshot on `dismiss`.
- `stagger = 30` — Delay increment in ms between consecutive visible children.
- `staggerFrom = .first` — Or `.last`. Order of stagger.

Rejected:

- `interaction Appear { on appear { … } }` — The `interaction` keyword is removed (PDL-E001). Put motion on `self.appear = { … }`.

```pdl
component Modal <PointerInput>() layout {
  let title = Text(content: "Hello")
  children = [title]
  self.appear = {
    animate = motion.appear
    from {
      opacity = 0
      scale = 0.95
    }
    stagger = 30
    staggerFrom = .first
  }
  self.dismiss = {
    animate = motion.dismiss
    to {
      opacity = 0
      scale = 0.95
    }
  }
}
```

## Samples

Reusable catalogs of instances you mount in layout so a prototype can stay interactive — a library of tracks, a set of chips, an empty list you can switch to. Write the catalog once and point at `Tracks.library.tracks` from a parameter default or from [`children`](#children). Isolated component examples, the kind you would put in design-system documentation, belong in fixtures.

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `samples Tracks { focus { tracks: [TrackRow] = [ … ] } }` | Declare a named catalog. A later `samples Tracks` replaces the earlier one. The name must not collide with a component. |
| `entry { field: Type = value }` | One named slice of the catalog (`focus`, `empty`). Fields are typed. An empty list is real data — no rows. |
| `Tracks.focus.tracks` | Point at one field: bank, then entry, then field. Use in defaults or layout so the prototype can switch data. |

```pdl
samples Tracks {
  library {
    tracks: [TrackRow] = [
      TrackRow(title: "Neon", trackId: "neon"),
      TrackRow(title: "Desk", trackId: "desk")
    ]
  }
  empty {
    tracks: [TrackRow] = []
  }
}

component SampleShelf(
  mood: MoodId = .all,
  tracks: [TrackRow] = Tracks.library.tracks
) layout {
  let list = Layout(direction: .column, children: [tracks])
  if mood == .focus {
    list.children = Tracks.empty.tracks
  }
  children = [list]
}
```

## Fixtures {#fixtures}

A fixture is a named bag of parameter values for one component. The Playground Fixture menu shows the labels. Each `example` is concrete values only — not other parameters, not layout. Flip through them to preview states without editing the component. Use fixtures for the examples you would put in design-system documentation — primary vs secondary, large vs small. Use them also for a whole view: empty search, a night playlist, mid-rename. Samples are the catalogs you mount; a fixture chooses which world the preview is in.

Write `fixtures Component { … }` next to the component (or inside [`extend`](#extend)). Each `example "Label" { … }` is one row in the Fixture menu. The body assigns that component’s parameters to concrete values — a string, a `.case`, a sample path. It does not write layout, and it does not read other parameters.

Accepted syntax:

- `fixtures Button { example "Primary" { … } }` — Named scenarios for one component. The quoted label is what you pick in the Fixture menu.
- `example "Secondary" { label = "Cancel" emphasis = .secondary }` — One scenario. Every assignment is a concrete value.
- `tracks = Tracks.empty.tracks` — A field may point at a sample. The fixture still chooses the world; the sample is the catalog.

Rejected:

- `example "X" { label = title }` — Not another parameter. Write a literal or a sample path.
- `fixtures Button { usage { description = "…" } }` — [`usage`](#usage), [`rules`](#rule), and [`extend`](#extend) are their own blocks. A fixtures block is only examples.

### Button variants

```pdl
variant Emphasis {
  case primary
  case secondary
}

component Button(
  label: String = "OK",
  emphasis: Emphasis = .primary
) layout {
  padding = 12
  background = #2563EB
  if emphasis == .secondary {
    background = #6B7280
  }
  let text = Text(content: label, color: #FFFFFF)
  children = [text]
}

fixtures Button {
  example "Primary" {
    label = "Save"
    emphasis = .primary
  }
  example "Secondary" {
    label = "Cancel"
    emphasis = .secondary
  }
}
```

### A playlist view

```pdl
samples Tracks {
  library {
    tracks: [TrackRow] = [
      TrackRow(title: "Neon", trackId: "neon"),
      TrackRow(title: "Desk", trackId: "desk")
    ]
  }
  focus {
    tracks: [TrackRow] = [
      TrackRow(title: "Desk", trackId: "desk")
    ]
  }
  empty {
    tracks: [TrackRow] = []
  }
}

enum MoodId {
  case all
  case focus
}

component Playlist(
  mood: MoodId = .all,
  query: String = "",
  tracks: [TrackRow] = Tracks.library.tracks
) layout {
  let list = Layout(direction: .column, children: [tracks])
  children = [list]
}

fixtures Playlist {
  example "Full library" {
    mood = .all
    tracks = Tracks.library.tracks
  }
  example "Focus" {
    mood = .focus
    tracks = Tracks.focus.tracks
  }
  example "Empty search" {
    query = "zzzz"
    tracks = Tracks.empty.tracks
  }
}
```

## Usage {#usage}

A written note on a component for authors and tools. In v1 the only key is `description`.

A written note attached to a component. Authors and tools read it; it does not change layout. In v1 the only key is `description`. Write `usage Button { … }` next to the component (or inside [`extend`](#extend)).

Accepted syntax:

- `usage Button { description = "…" }` — Replace the note. The name is the component, not a string.
- `description += " …"` — Append with a single space. Use this inside [`extend`](#extend) so a project can add a sentence without wiping the imported note.

Rejected:

- `usage Button { summary = "…" }` — Unknown keys are not defined in v1. Only `description`.
- `component Button() layout { usage { … } }` — `usage` is a top-level companion, not a frame property.

```pdl
usage Button {
  description = "Primary actions for forms. Prefer `emphasis = .primary` for one CTA per surface."
}
```

## Extend {#extend}

Add fixtures, usage, or rules to a component you imported — without copying its layout.

Add fixtures, usage, or rules to a component that already exists — usually one you imported — without copying its layout. Inner sections follow the same rules as standalone blocks. `description =` replaces; `description +=` appends. A later `tags =` replaces the whole tags array; [`Rule(…)`](#rule) lines append.

Accepted syntax:

- `extend Button { fixtures { example "…" { … } } }` — Add or replace a fixture by its label.
- `extend Button { usage { description += " …" } }` — Append to the imported note.
- `extend Button { rules { Rule(.should, …) } }` — Append a check. `tags =` in a later file replaces the tags array.

Rejected:

- `extend BannerTone { … }` — Only components. There is no `extend` for a variant or token.
- `extend Button { direction = .row }` — Extend does not edit layout. Change the source component, or wrap it.

```pdl
extend Button {
  fixtures {
    example "Project-specific" { label = "Submit request" }
  }
  usage {
    description += " In this project, always pair with a cancel action."
  }
}
```

## Rule {#rule}

A design check the preview or CI can flag. It does not change how anything looks. Tag instances in a `rules` block, then write a query from this instance — siblings, children, parent — and a strength ([`.must`](#rulestrength) fails the build; [`.should`](#rulestrength) warns).

Write `Rule(strength, query)` inside `rules Component { … }`. The query is true or false from this instance. [`.must`](#rulestrength) / [`.mustNot`](#rulestrength) fail validation; [`.should`](#rulestrength) / [`.shouldNot`](#rulestrength) warn. Optional `description:` is what authors see. `tags =` replaces the tag list; `tags.add` appends. An [`if`](#conditionals) in this block chooses tags and Rule lines from parameters — it does not restyle the frame. Rules-query [`self`](#self) is this instance, not layout [`self`](#self).

Accepted syntax:

- `rules Button { tags = ["button"]; Rule(.must, …) }` — Attach checks to a component. Tags are strings this instance can be found by.
- `Rule(.mustNot, siblings.where(tag: "primary-action").count > 0, description: "…")` — If the query matches, fail. Optional `description` is what authors see.
- `Rule(.should, self == parent.children.last, description: "…")` — A softer check. Rules-query [`self`](#self) is this instance — not layout [`self`](#self).
- `if emphasis == .primary { tags.add("primary-action") }` — Inside `rules`, [`if`](#conditionals) chooses tags and Rule lines from parameters. It does not restyle the frame.
- `Rule(.must, siblings.where(tag: "field-label").precedes(self), description: "…")` — Order in the parent’s children. Also `.follows` and `.adjacentTo`.

Rejected:

- `component Button() layout { tags = ["button"] }` — Tags are not frame properties. Put them in `rules`.
- `Rule(.must, …) in a layout body` — `Rule` is not a frame constructor. It only belongs in `rules`.

### One primary action

```pdl
variant Emphasis {
  case primary
  case secondary
}

component Button(
  label: String = "OK",
  emphasis: Emphasis = .primary
) layout {
  let text = Text(content: label)
  children = [text]
}

rules Button {
  tags = ["button"]

  if emphasis == .primary {
    tags.add("primary-action")
    Rule(.mustNot, siblings.where(tag: "primary-action").count > 0,
      description: "Only one primary button in this layout.")
  }
}
```

### How many tabs

```pdl
component Tab(label: String = "Tab") layout {
  let text = Text(content: label)
  children = [text]
}

rules Tab {
  tags = ["tab-item"]
}

component TabBar(tabs: [Tab] = [Tab(), Tab()]) layout {
  direction = .row
  children = [tabs]
}

rules TabBar {
  tags = ["tab-bar"]
  Rule(.must, children.where(tag: "tab-item").count.between(2, 5),
    description: "A tab bar must have between 2 and 5 tabs.")
}
```

### Sit last in the parent

```pdl
rules TabBar {
  tags = ["tab-bar"]
  Rule(.should, self == parent.children.last,
    description: "A tab bar should sit last among its siblings — usually the bottom of a column.")
}
```

### A label before the field

```pdl
component FieldLabel(content: String = "Name") text {
  content = content
}

rules FieldLabel {
  tags = ["field-label"]
}

component Field(value: String = "") layout {
  let text = Text(content: value)
  children = [text]
}

rules Field {
  tags = ["field"]
  Rule(.must, siblings.where(tag: "field-label").precedes(self),
    description: "A field must have a label sibling before it in the same parent.")
}
```

### Do not leave a card empty

```pdl
rules Card {
  tags = ["card"]
  Rule(.should, descendants.exists,
    description: "A card should contain at least one nested instance.")
}
```

Strengths are [`RuleStrength`](#rulestrength).

### Navigators

| Navigator | Meaning |
|-----------|--------|
| `self` | This component instance (the one whose [`rules`](#rule) block is running). |
| `parent` | The instance that contains this one. Empty at the design root. |
| `ancestors` | Walk upward toward the root. |
| `descendants` | Walk downward through nested instances. |
| `siblings` | Other children of the same parent. |
| `children` | Direct children only. |

### Filters

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `.where(tag: "name")` | Keep instances tagged with that name. Tags come only from [`rules`](#rule) blocks. |

### Aggregates

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `.exists` | True if any node matches. |
| `.count` | [`Number`](#number) of matches. |
| `.first / .last` | Optional node, for ordering predicates. |
| `.between(n, m)` | Inclusive range on a count. |

### Ordering

| Form | Meaning |
|------|------|
| `.precedes(self)` | Some match appears before self in the parent’s children order. |
| `.follows(self)` | Some match appears after self. |
| `.adjacentTo(self)` | Some match is immediately next to self. |
